jurisdiction_name: Douglas County PUD (PUD No. 1 of Douglas County)
summary: PUD commission halted new power contracts with data centers and crypto miners (non-diverse loads) to review rates; ended when new data center/crypto rates were adopted Jan 2020.
notes: End date = 2020-01-27 commission rate adoption; GovTech/Wenatchee World describe it as ending the eight-month moratorium. Board resolution not retrieved.

jurisdiction_name: Douglas County PUD (PUD No. 1 of Douglas County)
summary: Three-month moratorium on new bitcoin/data-mining loads while the PUD set terms; followed by a rate/contract structure for loads of 1.5 MW or more.
notes: Month not found; both sources are 2018 retrospectives. Sector described as data mining (bitcoin).

jurisdiction_name: Chelan County PUD (PUD No. 1 of Chelan County)
summary: Emergency moratorium on accepting or processing applications for new or increased cryptocurrency/high-density loads; extended May 2018, to Aug 6, Aug 20 and beyond while crypto rates were set.
notes: End date unverified: rate approval was slated for 2018-12-03 effective April 2019 (search snippet); chelanpud.org pages returned 403. MRSC notes the moratorium applied to service over 5 MW.

jurisdiction_name: Chelan County PUD (PUD No. 1 of Chelan County)
summary: First Chelan PUD moratorium on new cryptocurrency loads, 2014 to January 2017; 22 crypto applications were approved when it ended.
notes: Single secondary source; start month unknown.

summary: PUD put about 125 new (mostly crypto) service requests on hold in 2017; replaced by a two-queue process and above-cost Rate 17 for evolving industries (adopted 2018-08-28, effective 2019-04-01).
notes: Start date conflicts: MRSC says Nov 2017 'shelved all new service requests'; Tri-Cities Business News says applications put on hold 'last summer' (2017). Grant PUD's own June 2018 recap mentions no moratorium, so treat as an informal hold. End date = Rate 17 effective date.

summary: Interim load-growth caps on data center customers (Quincy industrial area) because demand exceeds transmission/distribution capacity; other customer classes may still grow.
notes: A cap on growth, not a halt on applications: the queue stayed open (75 applications later reported by APPA). Clearing Up dates the cap to 2025-04-01. Borderline for inclusion; listed because it limits new data center load.

summary: Commissioners stopped accepting applications for crypto mining/blockchain loads to study system impacts and a new rate structure; existing licensed operations unaffected.
notes: Adopted the last week of July 2018. End date and status not found; 'expired' is assumed and needs checking. Search snippets say data centers were covered too.

summary: Moratorium on accepting new service applications with energy use intensity above 250 kWh/sq ft/yr (aimed at crypto mining); hearing set for 2018-04-23, renewable in 60-day steps.
notes: Renewals and end not found; 'expired' is assumed.

summary: Moratorium on service to new computer/data processing loads for crypto mining, bitcoin or blockchain after a 10 MW request; approved applications exempt.
notes: Announced about 2018-04-11. End not found; 'expired' is assumed.

summary: Town-owned Massena Electric set its own moratorium on new cryptocurrency mining customers while it negotiated with three existing prospects; separate from the town's planned 90-day zoning moratorium.
notes: Exact adoption date and end not found; 'expired' is assumed. The Town of Massena zoning moratorium is a separate town-level action, not listed here.

summary: City council imposed an 18-month moratorium on new commercial crypto mining because miners were using 10-15% of the municipal utility's low-cost hydropower allocation; lifted about March 2019.
notes: An act of the city council (a local law), so it may belong in the city slice; listed here because the rationale was the city-owned electric utility's power allocation. Not in upstream. CRS cites AP 'City Lifts Ban' (2019-03-01). Search results also mention a new 12-month Plattsburgh moratorium proposed in 2026 (unverified; source unreachable).

summary: Dominion paused new data center connections in eastern Loudoun (Data Center Alley) over transmission limits; resumed incrementally in Sept 2022 with reduced allocations.
notes: Informal utility pause, not a commission order. Upstream's Loudoun County row (2026-09-16) is a separate county action.

summary: AEP Ohio halted new data center/crypto service agreements in central Ohio to study ~30 GW of requests; PUCO's 2025-07-09 data center tariff order required the moratorium to be lifted in phases.
notes: County list is approximate (central Ohio data center cluster: Columbus, New Albany, Dublin, Hilliard, Plain City). Lift tied to the effective date of the tariff; AEP filed final tariffs 2025-07-11.

service_area_counties: Maricopa; Yavapai; Coconino; Navajo; Apache; Yuma; Pinal; Gila; La Paz
summary: APS says it has made no commitments to serve new data center customers since Jan 1, 2024, citing grid constraints, especially overnight supply; projects already committed continue.
notes: No formal moratorium order found; this is a de facto halt on new commitments, per the utility's statement to KJZZ (2026-09-02). County list approximate: APS serves 11 of 15 Arizona counties, and data center demand is in Maricopa.

jurisdiction_name: Delaware Public Service Commission (Delmarva Power & Light territory)
duration: until a large-load tariff is approved
summary: PSC voted to open a large-load tariff docket and pause interconnection of new loads of 25 MW or more in Delmarva Power territory until a tariff is set; the pause was still in place as of March 2026.
notes: Oral vote 2025-09-03; written order at the 2025-10-15 meeting. Delmarva supported the pause. Final tariff decision expected after summer 2026 hearing examiner findings; no lift found as of 2026-10.

summary: The Governor directed PUCT and ERCOT to audit every data center in the ~474 GW interconnection queue before approving connections; ERCOT suspended Batch Zero large-load notifications.
notes: Instrument: the Governor's 2026-08-03 letter plus an ERCOT market notice (Batch Zero notifications due 2026-08-07 were suspended; good-cause exception sought at the PUCT's 2026-08-20 meeting). A separate Sept 2026 TCEQ permit pause is environmental permitting, not utility service, so it is not listed. Could arguably be type=executive order.
